A googol equals 10 to the power 100..why: The definition of the word; Wikipedia opens with it (10100 is 10 with the exponent 100 as a superscript on the page) and the exact phrase is common in Dolma.

sources.quote: A googol is the large number 10100 or ten to the power of one hundred.

A googol is a positive number..why: Any power of ten is positive.

A googol is smaller than one million..why: Deliberately false side fact: a googol is 10 to the power 100 (or, after the edit, 10 to the power 50), far more than a million.

notes: Dev ABox revision; edit property: chain and transitivity. Relation has_value (staging: functional, subproperty:equals, chains with has_digit_count, less_than, greater_than and has_cube): a named number has one value and compares and computes as that value does. Related near is the functional exclusion ('Is a googol equal to 10 to the power 100?'); it was the converse reading under 'symmetry' before review, but the 'no' comes from functionality, and the converse of the edit's own equation only restates it. The topic cannot supply a symmetry or inverse near question with a stored answer (see replace-d001). Related far is the popular comparison of a googol with the number of atoms in the observable universe (about 10^80): stored, two hops through the bridge, and it flips (10^50 is far smaller). The earlier far query (zeros after the 1) was a rewrite of the exponent and was dropped. Derived: a comparison with 10^60 (chain through less_than), equality with 100 to the power 25 (transitivity of equals: googol = 10^50 = 100^25), and the cube (an application, chain through has_cube: 10^300 becomes 10^150, which differs from both the old and the new value). Dropped after review: the digit count (off-by-one risk: 101 is often answered 100), the square root (its original answer, 10^50, is the edit's own target), and the base-10 logarithm (it is the direct question, 'what power of ten', in other words). Mathematics has no consistent world after an edit (README), so all queries are determinate; a model that recomputes from the definition 'googol = 10^100' is the failure being measured. Unrelated near asks who popularized the name (Edward Kasner; the name was coined by his nephew Milton Sirotta, so the question asks for the popularizer): same subject, untouched by the value. The earlier near query (the company named after a misspelling) gave its answer away. A googolplex question was rejected as near: its value moves with the googol. infini-gram was unreachable (HTTP 403) when the queries were revised on 2026-11-11, so new evidence is Wikipedia quotes and Wikipedia and web search hit counts. Revised 2026-11-12 after the model audit: the equality with 100 to the power 25 was dropped because 3 of 4 models denied that 10^50 equals 100^25; the second derived query now compares a googol with 10 to the power 70 (bridge held by comparing exponents). Related[1] was 'Is a googol equal to 10 to the power 50?', word for word the edit; it now names the same number in its written-out form (a 1 followed by fifty zeros), so it is not the edit sentence.
